question:
The general target of the monetary policy is to ensure __________.

A) price stability in the economy

B) greater tax collections for the government

C) employment generation in the rural areas
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The primary/general objective of monetary policy, as conducted by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), is to maintain price stability in the economy while keeping in mind the objective of growth. (मौद्रिक नीति — मूल्य स्थिरता)

 

• Under the amended RBI Act, 1934, the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) is mandated to maintain Consumer Price Index (CPI) inflation at 4% (+/- 2%).

 

• Statement A (price stability) correctly describes the general/core target of monetary policy; Statements B and C are objectives more closely associated with fiscal policy, not monetary policy.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Fiscal policy, controlled by the Ministry of Finance, deals with government revenue (taxation) and expenditure, and includes goals like employment generation and redistribution of income.

 

• Monetary policy uses tools such as the repo rate, reverse repo rate, CRR, and SLR to regulate money supply and control inflation.

 

NOTE

 

• Both B and C (Option 1): Incorrect, as neither "greater tax collections" nor "employment generation in rural areas" is the general target of monetary policy — both belong to fiscal policy.

 

• Only C (Option 2): Incorrect for the same reason; employment generation in rural areas is a fiscal/developmental policy goal.

 

• Both A and B (Option 3): Incorrect, since B (tax collection) is not a monetary policy target.

question: Which cytologist demonstrated the role of the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) in protein processing and sorting in a variety of cells in the 1960s?
solution_text:
The correct answer is George E Palade.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• George E. Palade (Romanian-American cell biologist) used electron microscopy in the 1960s to demonstrate how the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) and Golgi apparatus work together in the processing, packaging, and sorting of proteins in cells. (कोशिका विज्ञानी — जॉर्ज ई. पैलेड)

 

• For his pioneering work on the structural and functional organisation of the cell, particularly the secretory pathway, Palade shared the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1974 with Albert Claude and Christian de Duve.

 

• He is often called the "father of modern cell biology".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Albert Claude pioneered the use of the electron microscope and differential centrifugation for cell fractionation.

 

• Christian de Duve discovered the lysosome and peroxisome.

 

NOTE

 

• Ralph M Steinman (Option 1): Discovered the dendritic cell and its role in the adaptive immune response; won the Nobel Prize in 2011.

 

• Nettie Stevens (Option 3): An American geneticist known for discovering the XY sex-determination system.

 

• Cyril Darlington (Option 4): A British biologist known for his work on chromosome behaviour and cytogenetics.

question: As per the responsibilities defined in National Food Security Act, 2013, which of the following is a responsibility of the state/UT government?
option_1: Transportation of foodgrains up to designated depots in each state/UT
option_2: Allocation of required foodgrains to states/UTs
option_3: Delivery of foodgrains from designated FCI godowns
solution_text:
The correct answer is Identification of eligible households.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The National Food Security Act (NFSA), 2013 divides responsibilities between the Central and State/UT Governments for implementing the Targeted Public Distribution System (TPDS). (राष्ट्रीय खाद्य सुरक्षा अधिनियम — पात्र परिवारों की पहचान)

 

• State/UT Government responsibilities include: identification of eligible households, issuing ration cards, intra-state allocation and delivery of foodgrains from FCI godowns to Fair Price Shops (FPS), and ensuring the proper functioning of FPS.

 

• Central Government responsibilities include: allocation of foodgrains from the central pool to States/UTs, and transportation of foodgrains up to designated depots in each state/UT.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Under NFSA, up to 75% of the rural population and 50% of the urban population are covered, amounting to about two-thirds of India's total population.

 

• Eligible households are entitled to foodgrains at subsidised prices of ₹3/2/1 per kg for rice/wheat/coarse grains under the Priority Households and Antyodaya Anna Yojana categories.

 

NOTE

 

• Transportation of foodgrains up to designated depots (Option 1): This is a Central Government responsibility, not a state responsibility.

 

• Allocation of required foodgrains to states/UTs (Option 2): This is also a Central Government responsibility, done from the central pool.

 

• Delivery of foodgrains from designated FCI godowns (Option 3): This describes part of the intra-state distribution process; the Act specifically and distinctly assigns identification of the actual beneficiary households to the State/UT Government as the defining responsibility tested here.

question: At the Asian Wrestling Championships 2023 in Astana, Kazakhstan, who won silver in the 53 kg weight category?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Antim Panghal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• At the 2023 Asian Wrestling Championships, held in Astana, Kazakhstan in April 2023, Indian wrestler Antim Panghal won the silver medal in the women's 53 kg freestyle category. (एशियाई कुश्ती चैंपियनशिप 2023 — अंतिम पंघाल)

 

• India's other wrestlers — Anshu Malik, Sonam Malik, Manisha, and Reetika Hooda — won bronze medals at the same championship.

 

• Antim Panghal was earlier the first Indian woman to win a gold medal at the U-20 World Wrestling Championship (2022).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India finished the 2023 Asian Wrestling Championships with a total of 14 medals.

 

• The championship covers freestyle, Greco-Roman, and women's wrestling disciplines.

 

NOTE

 

• Reetika Hooda (Option 1): Won a bronze medal (76 kg category) at the same championship, not silver in 53 kg.

 

• Anshu Malik (Option 2): Won a bronze medal (57 kg category), not silver in 53 kg.

 

• Sonam Malik (Option 4): Won a bronze medal (62 kg category), not silver in 53 kg.

question: On which day was it announced that the Khel Ratna award will be declared as the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna award?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 6 August 2021.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• On 6 August 2021, Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced that India's highest sporting honour, the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award, would be renamed the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award, in honour of the legendary hockey player Major Dhyan Chand. (मेजर ध्यानचंद खेल रत्न पुरस्कार — 6 अगस्त 2021)

 

• The announcement came during the Tokyo Olympics 2020 (held in 2021), coinciding with India's hockey team's medal-winning campaign.

 

• Major Dhyan Chand's birthday, 29 August, is separately observed as National Sports Day in India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Khel Ratna Award is India's highest sporting honour, given for the most spectacular and outstanding performance in the field of sports over a four-year period.

 

• Major Dhyan Chand, known as the "Hockey Wizard", helped India win three consecutive Olympic hockey gold medals (1928, 1932, 1936).

 

NOTE

 

• 29 August 2020 (Option 1) and 29 August 2021 (Option 3): 29 August is celebrated as National Sports Day (Dhyan Chand's birthday), not the date the award was renamed.

 

• 6 August 2020 (Option 4): Incorrect date; the actual announcement was made on 6 August 2021, not 2020.

question: In which year did the Government of India bring FRBM (Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management) Act into effect?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2004-05.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act was enacted by Parliament in 2003 and came into effect/force from 5 July 2004, i.e., financial year 2004-05. (राजकोषीय उत्तरदायित्व और बजट प्रबंधन अधिनियम — 2004-05)

 

• The Act aims to ensure fiscal discipline by setting targets for reducing fiscal deficit and revenue deficit, and improving macroeconomic management and public fund management.

 

• The FRBM Rules were notified in July 2004 along with the Act's enforcement.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The FRBM Act, 2003 was later amended by the FRBM (Amendment) Act, 2018, which introduced fiscal deficit and debt targets (fiscal deficit of 3% of GDP by 2020-21).

 

• The N.K. Singh Committee (2016-17) reviewed the FRBM framework and recommended a debt-to-GDP anchor.

 

NOTE

 

• 2015-16 (Option 1), 2012-13 (Option 2), and 2008-09 (Option 4): These years do not correspond to when the FRBM Act was brought into effect; the Act's enforcement year is 2004-05.

question: Pushkar Mela is a popular cultural festival of which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajasthan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Pushkar Mela (Pushkar Camel Fair) is a famous annual cultural and livestock fair held in the town of Pushkar, in Ajmer district, Rajasthan. (पुष्कर मेला — राजस्थान)

 

• It is held every year in the Hindu month of Kartik (October-November), coinciding with Kartik Purnima, and is one of the world's largest camel and cattle fairs.

 

• Pilgrims also take a holy dip in Pushkar Lake, believed to be created by Lord Brahma, whose only major temple in India is located in Pushkar.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other famous fairs of Rajasthan include the Nagaur Fair and the Kolayat Fair.

 

• Rajasthan is also known for other cultural festivals like the Desert Festival (Jaisalmer) and Teej.

 

NOTE

 

• Assam (Option 1): Known for festivals like Bihu.

 

• Bihar (Option 2): Known for Chhath Puja and the Sonepur Mela (cattle fair).

 

• Sikkim (Option 4): Known for festivals like Losar and Saga Dawa.

question: The number of significant figures in 0.05800 are:
solution_text:
The correct answer is four.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In 0.05800, the leading zeros (before the first non-zero digit) are not significant — they only indicate the position of the decimal point. (सार्थक अंक — 0.05800 में चार सार्थक अंक)

 

• The significant digits start from the first non-zero digit 5, giving: 5, 8, 0, 0 — a total of 4 significant figures.

 

• Trailing zeros that appear after a decimal point are always considered significant, which is why the two zeros after "58" are counted.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Rules of significant figures: all non-zero digits are significant; zeros between non-zero digits are significant; leading zeros are never significant; trailing zeros are significant only if there is a decimal point.

 

• For example, 100 has only 1 significant figure, but 100.0 has 4 significant figures.

 

NOTE

 

• two (Option 1): Would be the count if only "5" and "8" were considered, incorrectly ignoring the significant trailing zeros.

 

• six (Option 3): Overcounts by including the two leading (non-significant) zeros.

 

• five (Option 4): Incorrect; there are only two digits before the decimal (both zeros, non-significant) and four significant digits after it.

question: Which of these is NOT a characteristic of durable goods?
option_1: They are capable of repetitive use.
option_2: They are not extinguished by immediate consumption.
option_3: They are meant for repetitive purchases.
option_4: They have a relatively long life.
solution_text:
The correct answer is They are meant for repetitive purchases.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Durable goods are goods that do not wear out quickly and can be used repeatedly over a long period, such as cars, refrigerators, and furniture. (टिकाऊ वस्तुएं — बार-बार खरीदी नहीं जातीं)

 

• Their key characteristics are: capable of repetitive use, not extinguished by immediate/single consumption, and having a relatively long life.

 

• Being "meant for repetitive purchases" is instead a characteristic of non-durable (perishable/consumable) goods, such as food items, which are consumed quickly and must be bought again and again.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Non-durable goods are consumed in one or a few uses and need frequent replacement (e.g., soap, milk, fruits).

 

• Durable goods are also called "consumer durables" in economic classification and are an important indicator of consumer spending and economic health.

 

NOTE

 

• They are capable of repetitive use (Option 1): This IS a genuine characteristic of durable goods.

 

• They are not extinguished by immediate consumption (Option 2): This IS a genuine characteristic of durable goods.

 

• They have a relatively long life (Option 4): This IS a genuine characteristic of durable goods.

question: As per In the year 2022, which Indian airport had the most passengers and aircraft movements?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Indira Gandhi International Airport (Delhi).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per data for the year 2022, Indira Gandhi International Airport (IGIA), Delhi, remained India's busiest airport, recording the highest number of passengers and aircraft movements. (इंदिरा गांधी अंतरराष्ट्रीय हवाई अड्डा — दिल्ली)

 

• IGIA has consistently ranked as India's top airport by both passenger traffic and aircraft movements for several years, including in post-pandemic recovery years like 2022.

 

• It is operated by Delhi International Airport Limited (DIAL), a GMR-led consortium.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport, Mumbai is typically India's second-busiest airport.

 

• Other major Indian airports include Kempegowda International Airport, Bengaluru and Rajiv Gandhi International Airport, Hyderabad.

 

NOTE

 

• Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport, Mumbai (Option 1): Ranked second in passenger traffic in 2022, not first.

 

• Rajiv Gandhi International Airport, Hyderabad (Option 2): A major airport but with lower traffic than Delhi.

 

• Kempegowda International Airport, Bengaluru (Option 4): A major airport but with lower traffic than Delhi.

question: In the Union Budget 2023-24, the Government of India has adopted Seven Priorities, which are termed as __________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Saptarishi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In the Union Budget 2023-24, presented by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman, the government identified seven priorities, collectively termed the "Saptarishi", guiding India through the "Amrit Kaal". (केंद्रीय बजट 2023-24 — सप्तर्षि)

 

• The Saptarishi priorities are: Inclusive Development, Reaching the Last Mile, Infrastructure and Investment, Unleashing the Potential, Green Growth, Youth Power, and Financial Sector.

 

• The term "Saptarishi" literally means the "seven great sages" in Indian tradition, symbolically used to represent the seven guiding priorities of the budget.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Union Budget 2023-24 also raised the income tax rebate limit under the new tax regime to ₹7 lakh.

 

• The term "Amrit Kaal" refers to the 25-year period leading up to India's 100th year of independence (2047).

 

NOTE

 

• Spatasiddanth (Option 1), Saptanga (Option 3), and Spatasutra (Option 4): These are not the terms used for the Budget 2023-24 priorities; the correct term used by the Finance Ministry is "Saptarishi".

question: According to Census of India 2011, which of the following States/Union Territories are in correct descending order of literacy rate?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala, Lakshadweep, Mizoram.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per Census of India 2011, Kerala recorded the highest literacy rate in the country at 93.91%, followed by the Union Territory of Lakshadweep at 91.85%, and the state of Mizoram at 91.33%. (जनगणना 2011 — केरल, लक्षद्वीप, मिजोरम)

 

• This sequence — Kerala > Lakshadweep > Mizoram — represents the correct descending (top three) order of literacy rate among Indian states/UTs in the 2011 Census.

 

• Goa (88.70%), Tripura (87.75%), and Puducherry (86.55%) followed after Mizoram in the ranking, with lower literacy rates.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• As per Census 2011, Bihar recorded the lowest literacy rate among Indian states, at 61.80%.

 

• India's overall literacy rate as per Census 2011 was 74.04% (82.14% for males and 65.46% for females).

 

NOTE

 

• Kerala, Goa, Maharashtra (Option 1): Incorrect order — Goa and Maharashtra rank below Lakshadweep and Mizoram in literacy rate.

 

• Kerala, Puducherry, Goa (Option 3): Incorrect order — Puducherry's literacy rate is lower than that of Lakshadweep and Mizoram.

 

• Kerala, Uttarakhand, Madhya Pradesh (Option 4): Incorrect order — both Uttarakhand and Madhya Pradesh have considerably lower literacy rates than Lakshadweep and Mizoram.

question: Which of the following ancient texts is a source to study Bharatanatyam?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Abhinaya Darpana.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Abhinaya Darpana ("The Mirror of Gesture"), written by sage Nandikeshvara, is one of the most important ancient Sanskrit texts serving as a primary source for the study of Bharatanatyam and other Indian classical dance forms. (अभिनय दर्पण — भरतनाट्यम)

 

• It systematically describes hand gestures (mudras/hastas), body movements, facial expressions (abhinaya), and postures used in classical dance.

 

• Along with the Natya Shastra by Bharata Muni, it forms one of the foundational texts of Indian classical dance and drama theory.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bharatanatyam originated in Tamil Nadu and is considered one of the oldest classical dance forms of India.

 

• Other classical dance forms of India include Kathak (UP), Odissi (Odisha), Kathakali and Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Manipuri (Manipur), and Sattriya (Assam).

 

NOTE

 

• Abhigyan Shakuntalam (Option 2): A Sanskrit play written by Kalidasa, based on the story of Shakuntala; not a dance treatise.

 

• Ashtadhyayi (Option 3): A Sanskrit grammar text written by Panini.

 

• Arthashastra (Option 4): A treatise on statecraft, economics, and military strategy written by Chanakya (Kautilya).

question: Which of the following items is NOT a part of the non-plan revenue expenditure of the government budget?
option_4: Central assistance for states and union territories
solution_text:
The correct answer is Central assistance for states and union territories.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under the earlier Plan/Non-Plan expenditure classification (used until it was discontinued from the 2017-18 Budget), non-plan revenue expenditure included routine, recurring items such as salaries and pensions, subsidies, and defence services (revenue component). (गैर-योजना राजस्व व्यय — राज्यों को केंद्रीय सहायता)

 

• Central assistance to states and union territories for implementing Five-Year Plan schemes was classified as Plan expenditure, not non-plan expenditure, since it was linked to developmental/plan schemes.

 

• The Plan/Non-Plan classification was replaced with the Revenue/Capital expenditure classification starting Budget 2017-18, following the merger of Plan and Non-Plan expenditures.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Non-plan expenditure broadly covered essential/obligatory government spending, both developmental and non-developmental.

 

• The government discontinued the Five-Year Plans and the Plan/Non-Plan classification following the abolition of the Planning Commission and its replacement with NITI Aayog in 2015.

 

NOTE

 

• Salaries and pensions (Option 1): A genuine component of non-plan revenue expenditure.

 

• Subsidies (Option 2): A genuine component of non-plan revenue expenditure.

 

• Defence services (Option 3): The revenue component of defence expenditure was classified as non-plan revenue expenditure.

question: What did the term 'bhoga' refer to during the medieval period?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Revenue assignments.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• During the early medieval period in India, the term 'bhoga' referred to revenue assignments — grants of land or the right to collect revenue, given to officials, chiefs, or religious/military functionaries in lieu of services rendered. (भोग — राजस्व निर्धारण, मध्यकालीन भारत)

 

• This system is often cited as evidence of Indian feudalism, where local chiefs and intermediaries were granted the right to enjoy (bhoga) the revenue/produce of land instead of receiving a cash salary.

 

• The term is related to the Sanskrit "bhoga" meaning "enjoyment," reflecting the beneficiary's right to enjoy the revenue/produce of the assigned land.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Related revenue terms of the period include "bhaga" (the king's share of agricultural produce) and "kara" (a periodic tax on cultivators).

 

• The broader system of assigning revenue rights to intermediaries is compared by historians (like R.S. Sharma) to the European feudal system, and is a key concept in the study of "Indian feudalism."

 

NOTE

 

• Donations to temples (Option 2): This is more accurately described by terms like devadana or temple grants, not 'bhoga'.

 

• A festival (Option 3): 'Bhoga' is a revenue/administrative term in this context, not the name of a festival.

 

• Religious function (Option 4): While 'bhoga' can also colloquially refer to a food offering to a deity in some regional/temple contexts, in the medieval administrative/historical sense tested here, it specifically denotes a revenue assignment.

question: The Koya movement in Malkangiri, during 1880, (now in Odisha) was led by:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tama Dora.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Koya movement (Koya rebellion) in Malkangiri, in 1880, was a tribal uprising against British colonial exploitation and the oppressive administrative system, led by Tama Dora. (कोया आंदोलन, मलकानगिरी 1880 — ताम दोरा)

 

• Malkangiri, then part of the composite Madras Presidency/Vizagapatam Agency tracts, is now a district in Odisha.

 

• The Koya tribe, an indigenous community inhabiting parts of present-day Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Chhattisgarh, has a long history of resistance movements against colonial and exploitative administration.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other notable tribal uprisings in the Odisha/Andhra tribal belt include the Rampa Rebellion (1922-24) led by Alluri Sitarama Raju.

 

• Tribal movements of this region were often triggered by restrictive forest laws, the podu (shifting cultivation) ban, and exploitation by outside traders and moneylenders (sahukars).

 

NOTE

 

• Ratna Naik (Option 1), Rindo Majhi (Option 3), and Dayanidhi Dharua (Option 4): These are not identified as the leader of the 1880 Koya movement in Malkangiri; the movement is specifically associated with Tama Dora.

question: Which of the following awards was presented to Guru Bipin Singh, a popular Manipuri dancer?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sangeet Natak Akademi Award.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Guru Bipin Singh (1918-2000) was a celebrated Manipuri dance guru, credited with systematising and popularising the Manipuri classical dance form and founding the Manipuri Nartanalaya. (गुरु बिपिन सिंह — संगीत नाटक अकादमी पुरस्कार)

 

• He was honoured with the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award, given by India's national academy for music, dance, and drama, in recognition of his contribution to Manipuri dance.

 

• He trained several renowned dancers, including the Jhaveri sisters (Darshana, Nayana, Ranjana, and Suverna Jhaveri), who helped bring Manipuri dance to national and international prominence.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Manipuri dance is one of the eight classical dance forms of India, characterised by graceful, fluid movements and themes based on Vaishnavite (Radha-Krishna) devotion.

 

• Other prominent Manipuri dance exponents include the Jhaveri sisters and Rajkumar Singhajit Singh.

 

NOTE

 

• Saraswati Samman (Option 1): A literary award given by the K.K. Birla Foundation, not associated with Guru Bipin Singh.

 

• Kalamandal Puraskar (Option 2): Not the award associated with Guru Bipin Singh.

 

• Padma Shri (Option 4): Not recorded among Guru Bipin Singh's honours; his defining national honour was the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award.

question: Zakir Hussain is associated with which musical instrument?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tabla.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ustad Zakir Hussain was one of India's most celebrated tabla players, renowned worldwide for his virtuosity and contributions to Indian classical and fusion music. (ज़ाकिर हुसैन — तबला वादक)

 

• He was the son of the legendary tabla maestro Ustad Alla Rakha, and received numerous honours including the Padma Shri (1988), Padma Bhushan (2002), and multiple Grammy Awards.

 

• He was known for collaborations with artists across genres, including the fusion group Shakti, founded with guitarist John McLaughlin.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other legendary tabla players include Ustad Alla Rakha and Pandit Kishan Maharaj.

 

• Zakir Hussain won multiple Grammy Awards, including for the album *Shakti* and *As We Speak*.

 

NOTE

 

• Santoor (Option 1): Associated with musicians like Pandit Shivkumar Sharma.

 

• Sitar (Option 2): Associated with musicians like Pandit Ravi Shankar and Ustad Vilayat Khan.

 

• Piano (Option 4): Not an instrument traditionally associated with Zakir Hussain, who was a tabla maestro.

question: The radius of curvature of a charged particle's passage in a homogeneous magnetic field is proportional to:
solution_text:
The correct answer is momentum of particle.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• When a charged particle moves through a uniform (homogeneous) magnetic field perpendicular to its velocity, it experiences a magnetic force that provides the centripetal force for circular motion. (आवेशित कण — चुंबकीय क्षेत्र में वक्रता त्रिज्या, संवेग के समानुपाती)

 

• Equating the magnetic force to the centripetal force: qvB = mv²/r, which simplifies to r = mv/(qB), i.e., the radius of curvature r is directly proportional to the particle's momentum (mv), and inversely proportional to its charge (q) and the magnetic field strength (B).

 

• This relationship is fundamental to devices like the cyclotron and mass spectrometer, which use magnetic fields to determine the momentum/mass of charged particles.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The formula r = mv/(qB) is also called the gyroradius or Larmor radius in plasma physics.

 

• A cyclotron uses this principle to accelerate charged particles in a spiral path using a combination of magnetic and electric fields.

 

NOTE

 

• Energy of particle (Option 1): The radius depends directly on momentum, not on kinetic energy.

 

• Charge of particle (Option 2): The radius is inversely proportional to charge, not directly proportional.

 

• Strength of the field (Option 4): The radius is inversely proportional to the magnetic field strength, not directly proportional.

question: At the 2023 Khelo India Youth Games, how many silver medals were won by Maharashtra?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 55.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• At the Khelo India Youth Games, held in Madhya Pradesh (Bhopal) in January-February 2023, Maharashtra topped the medal tally with a total of 161 medals, comprising 56 gold, 55 silver, and 50 bronze medals. (खेलो इंडिया यूथ गेम्स 2023 — महाराष्ट्र, 55 रजत पदक)

 

• This marked Maharashtra's continued dominance in the Khelo India Youth Games since its inception.

 

• Haryana finished as the runner-up in the overall medal tally at this edition.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Khelo India Youth Games is an annual multi-disciplinary grassroots sporting event for young athletes in India, launched in 2018 to identify and nurture sporting talent.

 

• Madhya Pradesh hosted this edition of the Games for the first time.

 

NOTE

 

• 50 (Option 1): Incorrect; this was Maharashtra's bronze medal count, not silver.

 

• 56 (Option 3): Incorrect; this was Maharashtra's gold medal count, not silver.

 

• 60 (Option 4): Does not match Maharashtra's actual silver medal count of 55.

question: Which of these is NOT among the reforms related to agriculture undertaken under the five year plans?
option_1: Introduction of the policy of 'land to the tiller'
option_2: Introduction of the Land Ceiling Act
option_3: Launch of the high yielding variety seed technology
solution_text:
The correct answer is Formation of Rent Authority Department.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under India's Five-Year Plans, several genuine agricultural and land reforms were undertaken, including the policy of 'land to the tiller' (abolishing intermediaries and granting ownership rights to actual cultivators), the Land Ceiling Act (fixing maximum landholding limits), and the High Yielding Variety (HYV) seed technology launched during the Green Revolution in the mid-1960s. (पंचवर्षीय योजनाएं — कृषि सुधार)

 

• "Formation of Rent Authority Department" is not a recognised/standard land or agricultural reform undertaken under the Five-Year Plans; it does not correspond to any actual historical land reform measure.

 

• The actual pillars of land reforms in India include: abolition of intermediaries, tenancy reforms, land ceiling, and consolidation of holdings.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Green Revolution, associated with agricultural scientist M.S. Swaminathan, introduced HYV seeds, chemical fertilizers, and irrigation, dramatically boosting foodgrain production starting in the mid-1960s.

 

• Tenancy reforms aimed at regulating rent, providing security of tenure, and conferring ownership rights on tenants.

 

NOTE

 

• Introduction of the policy of 'land to the tiller' (Option 1): A genuine land reform measure aimed at ending exploitative tenancy.

 

• Introduction of the Land Ceiling Act (Option 2): A genuine land reform measure that fixed the maximum land a person/family could hold.

 

• Launch of the high yielding variety seed technology (Option 3): A genuine agricultural reform that formed the core of the Green Revolution.

question: Which of the following is the primary factor contributing to the dryness of old wells?
option_3: A lot of boring pumps have been set up in the adjacent areas.
option_4: The ground surrounding the wells has been covered with a layer of vegetation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is A lot of boring pumps have been set up in the adjacent areas.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The primary reason old open wells dry up is the excessive extraction of groundwater through borewells/boring pumps installed in the surrounding/adjacent areas, which lowers the water table faster than it can naturally recharge. (पुराने कुओं का सूखना — बोरिंग पंप, भूजल स्तर में गिरावट)

 

• As modern borewells draw water from much deeper aquifers using motorised pumps, they deplete the groundwater that traditionally fed shallow open wells, causing the latter to dry up.

 

• This is a widely observed rural/environmental phenomenon in India linked to unregulated groundwater extraction and falling water tables.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India is one of the largest extractors of groundwater in the world, leading to concerns about groundwater depletion, especially in agriculturally intensive states like Punjab and Haryana.

 

• Measures like rainwater harvesting and watershed management are promoted to recharge groundwater and revive traditional water sources like open wells.

 

NOTE

 

• Wells have been covered (Option 1): Covering a well affects its accessibility but is not the primary cause of the underlying water source drying up.

 

• People have stopped utilising wells (Option 2): Non-use does not cause a well to dry up; in fact, disuse would have no direct depleting effect on the water table.

 

• The ground surrounding the wells has been covered with a layer of vegetation (Option 4): Vegetation cover is not identified as a primary cause of well-drying; excessive groundwater extraction is the dominant factor.

question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution is related to the Right to Freedom?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 19.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 19 of the Indian Constitution, under Part III (Fundamental Rights), guarantees the Right to Freedom, including the freedoms of speech and expression, assembly, association, movement, residence, and profession. (भारतीय संविधान — अनुच्छेद 19, स्वतंत्रता का अधिकार)

 

• The Right to Freedom is covered by Articles 19 to 22 of the Constitution, with Article 19 specifically enumerating the fundamental freedoms available to citizens (originally seven, before the right to property was removed from Part III by the 44th Amendment).

 

• These freedoms are subject to reasonable restrictions in the interests of sovereignty, public order, decency, morality, and security of the state.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Articles 20, 21, and 22 (also part of the Right to Freedom) deal with protection in respect of conviction for offences, protection of life and personal liberty, and protection against arrest and detention, respectively.

 

• The Right to Freedom is one of the six fundamental rights guaranteed under the Indian Constitution (originally seven).

 

NOTE

 

• Article 17 (Option 1): Deals with the abolition of untouchability, part of the Right to Equality group (Articles 14-18).

 

• Article 18 (Option 3): Deals with the abolition of titles, also part of the Right to Equality group.

 

• Article 16 (Option 4): Deals with equality of opportunity in matters of public employment, part of the Right to Equality.

question: What is the direction of the southeast trade winds in India during the southwest monsoon season?
solution_text:
The correct answer is South-westerly.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• During the southwest monsoon season, the southeast trade winds originating in the southern hemisphere cross the equator and enter the Indian subcontinent. (दक्षिण-पूर्वी व्यापारिक पवनें — दक्षिण-पश्चिमी मानसून)

 

• Upon crossing the equator, these winds are deflected to the right due to the Coriolis force (Ferrel's Law, operative in the Northern Hemisphere), which transforms their direction from south-easterly to south-westerly.

 

• These deflected winds are what constitute the southwest monsoon winds that bring the bulk of India's rainfall between June and September.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) shifting northward over the Indian subcontinent in summer is a key trigger for the onset of the southwest monsoon.

 

• The northeast monsoon (retreating monsoon), occurring in winter, brings winds from the opposite, north-easterly direction and causes rainfall mainly in Tamil Nadu.

 

NOTE

 

• South-easterly (Option 1): This describes the winds' original direction in the southern hemisphere, before they cross the equator and get deflected.

 

• North-westerly (Option 2): Not the resultant direction of the deflected trade winds.

 

• North-easterly (Option 4): This describes the direction of the winter/retreating (northeast) monsoon, not the southwest monsoon.

question: The Fundamental Rights have been guaranteed to protect the public from repressive state actions; judicial decisions tend to expand the scope of the word 'State' as defined by __________ of the Indian Constitution.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 12.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 12 of the Indian Constitution, which opens Part III (Fundamental Rights), defines the term 'State' for the purposes of Part III, ensuring that fundamental rights can be enforced against the specified authorities. (अनुच्छेद 12 — 'राज्य' की परिभाषा)

 

• As per Article 12, 'State' includes the Government and Parliament of India, the Government and Legislature of each state, and all local or other authorities within India or under the control of the Government of India.

 

• Over time, through various judicial decisions (e.g., Rajasthan State Electricity Board v. Mohanlal, Ajay Hasia v. Khalid Mujib), courts have expanded the scope of 'State' to include statutory and government-controlled bodies/instrumentalities, ensuring wider protection of fundamental rights against repressive state actions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 13 declares that any law inconsistent with or in derogation of Fundamental Rights shall be void, and defines 'law' for this purpose.

 

• The judicial test evolved to determine if a body is 'State' under Article 12 is the "instrumentality or agency" test, laid down in cases like Ajay Hasia.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 14 (Option 2): Guarantees the Right to Equality before Law, not the definition of 'State'.

 

• Article 15 (Option 3): Prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth.

 

• Article 13 (Option 4): Deals with laws inconsistent with Fundamental Rights being void, not the definition of 'State' — that is specifically Article 12's role.
